pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing items are 0 and a CHECK rejects 2.
test 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list only open items in id order.
test 'AC-3' marks 3,1 done and checks ✓ items in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks all items in id order with ✓ only on done.
test 'AC-5' asserts exact nav for each view and for /.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__ values; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

The AC was edited after the go (commit b40fd19) to 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a real step. A test named AC-7 exists, but the edited item is not valid and the edit has no recorded owner decision.
traffic/routes.json lists both views; test 'AC-8' checks it.

findings.what: Commit b40fd19 ('Follow-up edits') changed AC-7 after the owner's go by inserting '— verified by review: checked by hand' mid-sentence. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for this. The step 'checked by hand' demonstrates nothing, and it contradicts the real test that proves AC-7. The edit also breaks the sentence's wording.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-7 edit so the item reads as at the go. Rely on the 'AC-7' test. If the owner really wanted a change, record it as a dated decision.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit edited acceptance item AC-7 after the go.
findings.fix: After reverting the edit, keep the claim. Otherwise list the AC-7 change and the owner's decision.

lenses.note: A spec exists with a go; the implementation follows both decisions (open by default, query parameter).
The States rows each have a test. AC-7 was edited after the go with no decision.
